transcript.text: Confirmed this mirrors the existing "house tier" pattern (customers.tier joined to orders.customer_id, grouped, counted). Now saving the "value tier" definition (fewest orders) linked to the same two datasets.

args.content: Working definition: the 'value tier' is the customer tier (customers.tier) that placed the FEWEST orders. It is derived, not a stored flag: join memory.bench.orders.customer_id to memory.bench.customers.customer_id, group by customers.tier, count orders per tier, and the tier with the LOWEST order count is the 'value tier'. This is the inverse of the 'house tier' (which uses the highest order count). Use this exact definition for any 'value tier' analysis in future sessions.
